name: Asahel
overview: Asahel was a male figure noted for his opposition to Israel's decision to set apart foreign wives, as recorded in Ezra 10:15. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided about him. His stance reflects a concern for maintaining Israelite purity in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Asahel means 'G-d [El] has made,' indicating a recognition of divine agency in his identity. This proper name, mentioned in Ezra 10:15, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jonathan as Asahel's father, inferred from the same verse in Ezra 10:15. No other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Asahel's importance lies in his role during the post-exilic period when Israel was addressing the issue of foreign marriages. His opposition to the inclusion of foreign wives aligns with the community's efforts to uphold covenant faithfulness and purity. Through his stance, Asahel exemplifies the concern for obedience to God's commands and the preservation of Israel's distinct identity.
